meta.date: From Com down to the birth of Ether
meta.unit: Prophets rejected, and the line down to Ether (Ether 11)
principles: A king who sheltered the men his people wanted dead
A destruction announced before it arrives

world_behind.title: Prophets come in three separate reigns
world_behind.text: Verses 1, 12, and 20 put prophets in the reigns of Com, Ethem, and Coriantor. Ether 7:23, 9:28 and 13:2 are the other places the book records preaching, so six reigns out of about thirty get prophets and the rest of the line passes without one.

world_behind.title: One king took them in
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has them flee to Com for protection when the people sought their lives.

world_behind.title: The next generation reversed that
world_behind.text: Verse 5 has the brother of Shiblom put the prophets to death.

world_behind.title: The coming destruction is called unmatched twice
world_behind.text: Verses 6 and 7 each set the coming destruction past anything the earth had seen. Ether 15:2 reports nearly two millions of mighty men slain besides their families, and Omni 1:22 has the people of Zarahemla reading the same account off a stone. The superlative is checked twice inside the record.

world_behind.title: A repentance is recorded mid-collapse
world_behind.text: Verse 8 says the people began to repent and the Lord had mercy inasmuch as they did. Ether 9:34 and 35 record the one earlier occasion the same thing happened, when a famine drove them to it. Two repentances are reported in fifteen chapters, and both are extracted by catastrophe.

world_behind.title: Two mighty men rise in one chapter
world_behind.text: Verses 15 and 17 each raise a mighty man against Moron, and the second is a descendant of the brother of Jared. Ether 6:25 has the brother of Jared's own firstborn refuse the crown; his line reaches the throne here by force, nine generations later.

world_behind.title: Ether is born into captivity
world_behind.text: Verse 23 has Coriantor beget Ether and then die still in captivity. Ether 10:30 to 31 lists five generations before him who lived their whole lives the same way, so the man who writes the record of this people is the first of his line in six generations to be free.

words.text: To leave off and walk away from. Treated at 3 Nephi 5:3. The record uses the word seven times and the King James Bible fifty-eight.
Shelter from harm. It appears seven times in the record and once in the King James Bible, at Deuteronomy 32:38. Verse 2 has prophets seeking it from a king.
A disaster falling on a whole people. Treated at Mormon 2:27. It appears three times in the record and nineteen in the King James Bible.
Piles left where something was gathered or dumped. It appears four times, twice in Ether, in the record, and the King James Bible twenty. Verse 6 applies it to bones.
Widespread deadly sickness. Treated at Alma 45:11. The record has it three times, the King James Bible twice.
Completely, to the last. The record uses the word eighteen times and the King James Bible a hundred and one. Verse 12 attaches it to destruction from off the face of the earth.
Pulled back and left. The word turns up six times here, and the King James Bible six. Verse 13 has prophets do it after the hearts hardened.

phrases.term: Except they should repent, and turn unto the Lord, and forsake their murders
phrases.text: The terms, given in three steps. Murder is named first among the things to leave.

phrases.term: They fled unto Com for protection
phrases.text: Where the prophets went when the people turned on them. The king was the shelter.

phrases.term: All the prophets who prophesied of the destruction of the people should be put to death
phrases.text: The order given by the brother of Shiblom. The offense named is the content of the message.

phrases.term: Their bones should become as heaps of earth upon the face of the land
phrases.text: The image the prophets used. Mormon 6:15 reports the Nephite version of the same scene.

phrases.term: They hearkened not unto the voice of the Lord, because of their wicked combinations
phrases.text: The reason given for the refusal. The combinations are treated as the obstacle.

phrases.term: Inasmuch as they did the Lord did have mercy on them
phrases.text: Mercy stated as a measure. The verse ties it to how far they came.
Four words closing the reign of Ahah. Verse 10 has already said what he did with them.

phrases.term: The prophets mourned and withdrew from among the people
phrases.text: What they did when the hearts hardened. Both verbs are given, in that order.

phrases.term: There arose a mighty man among them in iniquity
phrases.text: The description of the first challenger. Verse 17 raises a second, from a different line.

phrases.term: He was a descendant of the brother of Jared
phrases.text: The pedigree given to the second mighty man. Moroni supplies it without naming him.

phrases.term: Bring forth another people to possess the land
phrases.text: The promise the last prophets carried. Verse 21 says it would be done as their own fathers were brought.

verses.label: v. 1–23
verses.title: A chapter measured in reigns
verses.text: Days is used fourteen times across twelve of these twenty-three verses, almost always in the same construction: in the days of Com, in his days, all his days, all the remainder of his days. It is the chapter's only unit of time. No year is given anywhere, no season, and no interval between events. A stretch of history covering at least six kings is reported entirely as a sequence of lifetimes, and the reader can date nothing in it except relative to a man.

verses.label: v. 8
verses.title: One sentence of mercy in twenty-three verses
verses.text: The single relief in the chapter is stated and then dropped: "the people began to repent of their iniquity; and inasmuch as they did the Lord did have mercy on them." Nothing follows from it. The next verse kills the king and takes his successor into captivity, and repentance is not mentioned again. The clause is conditional in both directions, inasmuch as they did, which lets the mercy be reported without any claim that it lasted.

verses.label: v. 21
verses.title: A people told they will be replaced by their own method
verses.text: The last prophetic message in the chapter is not destruction but substitution: "the Lord God would send or bring forth another people to possess the land, by his power, after the manner by which he brought their fathers." The clause at the end is the point. The means of the replacement is stated to be the means of the original arrival, which sends a reader back to Ether 1:41–43 and the packing list. A nation is warned that the event which founded it will happen again to someone else.

verses.label: v. 23
verses.title: The writer of the book is born in a prison
verses.text: The chapter's last sentence produces its author and buries him in a subordinate clause: "Coriantor begat Ether, and he died, having dwelt in captivity all his days." The he is Coriantor. Ether, whose record this whole book is drawn from and who is named in Ether 1:6 as the man who wrote it, enters the narrative as the son of a man who never left captivity. Nothing is said here about the son at all beyond his existence.

chapter.title: The same sequence runs three times
chapter.text: Verses 1, 12, and 20 each bring prophets, and verses 2, 13, and 22 each record the rejection.

chapter.title: A king can be the shelter
chapter.text: Verse 2 has the prophets run to Com, and verse 3 says he was blessed all the rest of his days.

chapter.title: The next reign undoes it
chapter.text: Verse 5 has Shiblom's brother order the same men killed.

chapter.title: The warning is about bones
chapter.text: Verse 6 pictures them as heaps of earth spread on the land.

chapter.title: Repentance still works during the collapse
chapter.text: Verse 8 grants mercy in the measure they turned, in the middle of the worst destruction.

chapter.title: A whole reign fits in four words
chapter.text: Verse 10 closes Ahah with few were his days.

chapter.title: Prophets are allowed to leave
chapter.text: Verse 13 has them mourn and withdraw once the hearts were hard.

chapter.title: The land is promised to someone else
chapter.text: Verse 21 says another people would be brought the way their own fathers were brought.

applications.title: Shelter the person carrying the message
applications.text: The prophets ran to Com and Com took them in.

applications.title: Receiving them was the whole of what he did
applications.text: The prophets prophesied many things to Com, and the verse says he was blessed in all the remainder of his days. He is credited with no reform and no campaign, only with having taken them in and listened.

applications.title: Killing the messenger does not cancel the message
applications.text: The brother of Shiblom had every prophet who spoke of the destruction put to death, and the destruction arrived on schedule. Removing the people who said a thing changes nothing about whether it was true.

applications.title: What you are committed to sets what you can hear
applications.text: They hearkened not unto the voice of the Lord because of their wicked combinations. Prior commitments do most of the filtering long before anybody weighs an argument.

applications.title: Mercy is measured against the turn
applications.text: The verse ties the Lord's mercy to how far the people came.

applications.title: Know when to withdraw
applications.text: The prophets mourned and left instead of pressing a hardened people.

applications.title: Read the warning about your own ground
applications.text: The land was promised to another people on the terms the first people were given.

applications.title: A whole life in captivity, and then Ether
applications.text: Coriantor dwelt in captivity all his days, and the last thing recorded of him is that he begat Ether. Some lives leave nothing you can point at except the next person, and the book treats that as enough.

questions.text: Who has come to me for shelter?
What have I wanted silenced because of what it said?
What warning have I heard so often that it stopped landing?
Where has mercy already met a small turn of mine?
If my days were summed in four words, what would they say?
What have I hardened myself against?
What am I refusing because of the company I keep?

targets.verse_text: And there came prophets in the land again, crying repentance unto them—that they must prepare the way of the Lord or there should come a curse upon the face of the land; yea, even there should be a great famine, in which they should be destroyed if they did not repent.
targets.markdown: And **there came prophets in the land again, crying repentance unto them—that** they must prepare the way of the Lord or there should come a curse upon the face of the land; yea, even there should be a great famine, in which they should be destroyed if they did not repent.

entries.head: Ether 8:22

targets.verse_text: And whatsoever nation shall uphold such secret combinations, to get power and gain, until they shall spread over the nation, behold, they shall be destroyed; for the Lord will not suffer that the blood of his saints, which shall be shed by them, shall always cry unto him from the ground for vengeance upon them and yet he avenge them not.
targets.markdown: And **whatsoever nation shall uphold such secret combinations, to get power and gain**, until they shall spread over the nation, behold, they shall be destroyed; for the Lord will not suffer that the blood of his saints, which shall be shed by them, shall always cry unto him from the ground for vengeance upon them and yet he avenge them not.
